On 16 March 2017, at approximately 12:30 p.m. at the Alexis de Tocqueville high school ( French : Lycée Alexis de Tocqueville ) in the town of Grasse, France, a mass shooting occurred when a student opened fire, injuring four people. The attacker also use one of two homemade grenades during the attack, which failed to detonate.

The incident was the first mass school shooting in France since the Ozar Hatorah school shooting in 2012. Unlike the 2012 killings, committed by someone with no connection to the school, the identified perpetrator was a pupil at the school itself.
